 3:46 pm, November 8, 2026 Late-night chaos caps wild Saturday slate
 Good morning college football fans!
 Hope you got some rest after one of the best Saturday slates of the season. In case you missed any of the late-night scores from yesterday, we got you covered. Four of the five games we were tracking came down to one score. Check them out below:
 No. 15 Texas Tech survived West Virginia, 53-48 
 Hawaii edged UTEP, 17-14 
 Utah State bested Fresno State, 17-10 
 Texas State dominated Oregon State, 42-21 
 Wyoming took down UNLV, 41-35 
 No. 15 Texas Tech's 53-48 win over West Virginia was the key contest to cap a crazy day in college football. The Red Raiders took a 41-27 lead at half, at the hands of NINE  combined touchdowns — two of which were 70+ yarders. 
 The Mountaineers battled in the second half, shutting out a red-hot Raiders offense in the third quarter while limiting them to just 12 total yards. On the other side of the ball, WVU quarterback Michael Hawkins orchestrated three touchdown drives to go on a 21-0 run and gain the 48-41 lead. 
 The script flipped once again in the fourth quarter, as Stone Harrington completed a 46-yard field goal. TTU quarterback Tommy Castellanos connected with Kenny Johnson for a 5-yard touchdown pass to cap a 15-play, 69-yard drive that left 2:44 on the clock with the Raiders up by three. 
 WVU failed to answer on the ensuing drive as Hawkins was sacked in the Mountaineers ' end zone to give Texas Tech a safety and the ultimate 53-48 lead. 
 The Raiders recovered their onside kick to seal their dramatic victory. 
 share with Facebook copy link 4:37 am, November 8, 2026 👋 Signing off for the night
 We knew a weekend with seven ranked-vs.-ranked matchups wouldn't disappoint. Here's what you may have missed:
 Must-know results
 Here are some of the top ranked results from the day.
 No. 11 Notre Dame escaped No. 1 Miami (FL) 31-24 
 No. 2 Georgia blasted No. 10 Ole Miss 42-7 
 No. 3 Utah took down rival No. 9 BYU 28-20 
 No. 5 Alabama handled No. 14 LSU 31-13 
 No. 13 Tennessee routed No. 6 Kentucky 34-6 
 No. 7 Texas beat No.18 Missouri 34-20 
 No. 23 Oregon stunned No. 12 Ohio State 41-28 
 Oklahoma upset No. 24 Florida 23-7 
 The action didn't end with FBS ranked stunners. The FCS had some of the top teams on the ropes. It'll surely shake up the next rankings.
 No. 1 Tarleton State beat No. 22 Abilene Christian 40-27 to stay undefeated 
 No. 12 Lamar handed No. 2 Stephen F. Austin its first loss of the season 45-28 
 No. 3 Montana State escaped No. 18 Idaho State 28-26 in 3OT 
 No. 15 North Dakota cooked No. 8 Illinois State 49-21 
 No. 13 Montana saw RB Eli Gillman break Cooper Kupp's Big Sky total TD record in a 57-24 win over Portland State 
 Prairie View A&M knocked off the top HBCU team No. 24 Alabama A&M 31-10 
 Even at the Division II and Division III level there were record-breaking days. DII Ferris State tied the DII record for consecutive wins at 40 and DIII Endicott scored 93 points.
 Games still going on
 After all of those games, can you imagine that there's more football to watch? Here's what's left to close the night after 12 a.m. E.T.:
 No. 15 Texas Tech vs. West Virginia 
 Hawaii at UTEP 
 Fresno State at Utah State 
 Texas State at Oregon State 
 Wyoming at UNLV 
 Looking ahead to the CFP Rankings
 The second College Football Playoff rankings are coming after this week. Here's some quick takeaways at the top of the rankings after today's results:
 No. 1 Miami will fall after losing to No. 11 Notre Dame. The game was close, and the committee had Miami at the top despite metrics like strength of schedule. The Hurricanes also have a win over a Wake Forest team to serve as a floor. Miami likely stays top 10.
 No. 2 Georgia could slot into the No. 1 spot. The Bulldogs do have one loss, but they just dominated No. 10 Ole Miss.
 No. 3 Utah has the best argument to prevent UGA from grabbing No. 1. The Utes are undefeated at added a top-10 win over No. 9 BYU.
 No. 5 Alabama will likely remain the highest ranked two-loss team after adding a ranked win over No. 14 LSU. That is... unless Tennessee's win moves them into the same pod.
 No. 6 Kentucky  was dominated by Tennessee and now have two losses. The metrics liked Kentucky last week, but will the Wildcats remain in the projected bracket after losing by 28 points?
 No. 7 Texas  won its third-straight game after losing back-to-back games in the middle of the season. The Longhorns moved to 4-0 against ranked opponents this season with a 34-20 win over No. 18 Missouri. Texas might enter the top five.
 No. 8 UCLA  moved to 9-0 with a 14-point win over Minnesota. Despite the undefeated record, the Bruins could get leapfrogged by Notre Dame and Tennessee after both picked up top-10 wins. However, it all could keep UCLA at No. 8 since two teams likely drop below it.
 No. 9 BYU's  placement in the rankings will be interesting after losing to Utah. The Cougars lost, but they also have a head-to-head win over Notre Dame. Could BYU end up moving up after a loss?
 No. 11 Notre Dame  just knocked off the No. 1 team. How high will the Fighting Irish rise? Will Notre Dame move past a BYU team it lost to? There's a lot that's at stake in the upcoming rankings.
 No. 12 Ohio State  isn't officially eliminated from the CFP, but after losing back-to-back games for the first time since 2011, it's a long stretch. Some are wondering if Ohio State will even be ranked, but a win over Indiana should allow the Buckeyes to hold on. We think...
 No. 13 Tennessee  is almost a lock to join the top-10 this week. The Vols blasted No. 6 Kentucky, and also have a win over Alabama on its resume. The question facing Vol fans is whether or not the Kentucky win is enough to move UT into the same pod as an Alabama team it beat.
 share with Facebook copy link 4:21 am, November 8, 2026 Texas Tech and West Virginia are LIGHTING UP the scoreboard
 Now that we’re all done watching Notre Dame take down Miami, you should flip the channel over to ESPN for No. 15 Texas Tech vs. West Virginia, where the Red Raiders lead, 41-27 . 
 Since we began writing this post, we’ve seen FOUR touchdowns. We’ve seen NINE total touchdowns — two of which were 70+ yarders — while three others were 29+ yards.  
 Oh yeah, and those were all in the first half . 
 That’s right. The Mountaineers and Red Raiders are trading blows like heavyweight fighters out in Lubbock. Texas Tech opened the scoring with a 30-yard TD pass before West Virginia answered, then took the lead with a field goal. 
 They traded TDs two more times — including the two 70-yarders — before Texas Tech tacked on three more unanswered TDs before the end of the half. 
 Shot out of a cannon ✌️ 📺: ESPN https://t.co/N2TkfZM48J
— Texas Tech Football (@TexasTechFB) November 8, 2026 
 Hello, Taron 👋 📺 ESPN https://t.co/i5E81kQn1k
— West Virginia Football (@WVUfootball) November 8, 2026 
 The quarterbacks are both throwing bombs. Texas Tech QB Thomas Castellanos is 10-for-13 for 287 yards and four touchdowns, while West Virginia QB Michael Hawkins Jr. is 5-for-8 for 183 yards and a TD.  
 WVU has another 215 yards on the ground, with two rushing touchdowns. Texas Tech has 207 yards and two TDs on the ground.
 Wild stuff is happening over in the Big 12.
 share with Facebook copy link 4:09 am, November 8, 2026 No. 1 Miami falls to Notre Dame
 Down goes No. 1!
 No. 11 Notre Dame knocked off No. 1 Miami 31-24 in South Bend. The Fighting Irish avenged last year’s loss, holding off a second-half rally from the Hurricanes.
 Notre Dame jumped out to a 24-3 lead in the third quarter after three touchdown passes from CJ Carr. However, Miami fought back after Darien Mensah threw three touchdowns of his own — all in the second half. 
 A 20-yard dart to @Gilbert316Micah for the touchdown 🎯 #GoIrish☘️ | @13Cjcarr 📺: NBC https://t.co/ZNcye9QBtf
— Notre Dame Football (@NDFootball) November 8, 2026 
 Then came Miami’s fourth quarter drive. Miami faced a fourth-and-six at Notre Dame's 18-yard-line. Mensah found tight end Eli Lofton in the corner of the end zone, but the tight end couldn’t add to his seven-catch, 113-yard and one touchdown day. Lofton couldn’t maintain possession of the ball and Miami turned the ball over on downs with 3:36 left to play
 Rules analyst Terry McAulay breaks down what makes this PIVOTAL play an incomplete pass. 📺 Notre Dame Football on NBC & Peacock https://t.co/9pso7otXoG
— NBC Sports (@NBCSports) November 8, 2026 
 Notre Dame tried to run its four-minute-offense, but ended up punting the ball back to the Hurricanes with 57 seconds on the clock. It wasn’t enough for Miami to find success, as a hook-and-ladder fell short.
 The loss knocks Miami from the unbeaten ranks, leaving just Utah and UCLA with zeros in the loss column .
 Notre Dame now leads the all-time series 18-9-1 dating back to 1955.
 share with Facebook copy link 2:40 am, November 8, 2026 No. 13 Tennessee crushes No. 6 Kentucky at home
 Speaking of SEC blowouts, No. 13 Tennessee just crushed No. 6 Kentucky in Knoxville, 34-6. Tennessee gets its second top-10 win of the season, knocking off its rival and likely rocketing into the top-10 CFP rankings on Tuesday. 
 It was an efficient night for the Volunteer offense, with the first touchdown coming on the first play of the Vols’ third drive, a 66-yard run by Duane Morris. 
 Absolute CINEMA from the Sky Cam on the Duane Morris 66 yard TD run https://t.co/xfthXd1cAT
— gmannVOLS (@gmannVOLS) November 7, 2026 
 Kentucky narrowed the deficit to four points before the half, but that would do it for the Wildcats’ offense. Tennessee held Kentucky scoreless in the second half, while the Volunteers piled on three touchdowns in the fourth quarter. 
 QB George MacIntyre went 9-for-14 for 125 yards, and Faizon Brandon threw one pass for a 24-yard TD, but the story of the game was the Volunteers' rushing attack, which went for 240 yards and three total TDs. RB DeSean Bishop had 25 carries for 109 yards and two TDs.
 share with Facebook copy link 2:11 am, November 8, 2026 No. 2 Georgia making a statement at halftime
 No. 1 Miami might be on the ropes at halftime, but the No. 2 team in the country is doing the opposite.
 No. 2 Georgia is routing No. 10 Ole Miss 28-0 at halftime . The Bulldogs have shut down Heisman candidate quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, limiting him to only a 47% completion for just 69 yards and an interception. Ole Miss only has 37 rushing yards, while UGA has gained 183 on over seven yards per carry in the first half.
 If No. 1 Miami (FL) goes down today against No. 11 Notre Dame, Georgia is making a great case to be the next team at the top thanks to having the largest halftime lead on a top-10 opponent in program history during the CFP era.
 58-yard TD strike to Talyn Taylor 💥 📺: ABC https://t.co/4PIjBnfYCb
— Georgia Football (@GeorgiaFootball) November 8, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 1:57 am, November 8, 2026 No. 11 Notre Dame is pacing No. 1 Miami at halftime
 In perhaps the biggest game of the night for CFP implications, No. 11 Notre Dame is up 17-3 on the top team in the nation.  
 The first touchdown came on a beautiful 27-yard toe-tapping catch by Jordan Faison at the beginning of the second quarter. 
 Just look at that technique 😮‍💨 #GoIrish☘️ | @Jordan6Faison 📺: NBC https://t.co/CnFa4aDlUg
— Notre Dame Football (@NDFootball) November 8, 2026 
 The Notre Dame defense has held Miami to just 145 total yards — Darian Mensah is 6-for-12 passing for just 49 yards, and the Miami run game has just 96 yards. In the second quarter, the Irish made a huge goal-line stand on third-and-goal inside the five-yard line, forcing a Miami field goal. 
 CJ Carr, meanwhile, is 18-for-26 for 205 yards and two touchdowns, and he led a flawless two-minute drive at the end of the half to give Notre Dame a 14-point lead. 
 Slideee @Gilbert316Micah 😁 #GoIrish☘️ 📺: NBC https://t.co/n0zvbgv64i
— Notre Dame Football (@NDFootball) November 8, 2026 
 An interesting note: it's around 36 degrees in South Bend right now — Miami QB Darian Mensah has yet to win a road game in his career when the temperature falls below 55 degrees.
 With Duke 2025 — loss to UConn, Mensah 2 INT + fumble
 With Tulane 2024 — loss to Army, Mensah 1 INT + fumble
 share with Facebook copy link 1:27 am, November 8, 2026 Must-see game-winning TD in the Big 12
 The Big 12 started the day with a top-10 matchup but the game after dark might've had the best finish. UCF knocked off Kansas 33-32 after a game-winning touchdown. The Knights drove 73 yards in one minute to cap off a fourth quarter that saw Kansas score 18 points. 
 Watch the final drive below.
 Stop what you're doing and watch this game-winning drive 🫵 https://t.co/6sRDczMWMs
— UCF Football (@UCF_Football) November 8, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 12:47 am, November 8, 2026 Lamar wins a top-10 FCS clash
 The Southland conference's automatic bid to the FCS playoffs could've been clinched today, but thanks to Lamar, the first FCS auto-bid will have to wait another week.
 No. 12 Lamar took down No. 2 Stephen F. Austin 45-28 , handing the Lumberjacks their first loss of the 2026 season. The result moves both teams to one loss in conference play, and Lamar now owns the head-to-head tiebreaker with just two weeks remaining.
 After SFA's loss, only Tarleton State remains undefeated among FCS team. The Texans are currently taking on Abilene Christian .
 HE DID WHAT??? - Al Michaels Here's another look at Blake Thomas' TD catch. @ESPNAssignDesk #SCTop10 #ALLIN | #PeckEmCards https://t.co/j8ApRerAqb
— Lamar University Football (@LamarFootball) November 8, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 12:16 am, November 8, 2026 Oregon stuns Ohio State, Alabama handles LSU to start the night
 Ohio State's struggles continue
 No. 23 Oregon scored 38 unanswered points to comeback from a 14-0 deficit to land a convincing 41-28 win over No. 12 Ohio State . It's Oregon's second ranked win in as many weeks, building late season momentum in Eugene after a rough start to the season.  
 Ohio State was still without its starting quarterback Julian Sayin, and backup quarterback Luke Fahey had to throw 50 passes in the loss. Fahey went 36-of-50 for 360 yards and two touchdowns to one interception. However, the offense often sputtered as shown by visible frustration from Heisman contender Jeremiah Smith as he caught seven passes for 133 yards and a touchdown. 
 Here's a few facts about Ohio State's loss: 
 Dating back to last year, Ohio State is 6-5 in their last 11 games.
 It's the first time Ohio State has lost three games in a season since 2011 — that was the year Jim Tressell resigned in May.
 2011 is also the last time Ohio State lost back-to-back games.
 Meanwhile, win keeps Oregon's Big Ten Championship Game hopes alive. The Ducks are 4-2 in conference play so with some help down the stretch, can still be alive for the College Football Playoff with three losses. 
 DAKORIEN MOORE ONE-HANDED GRAB TOUCHDOWN 🤯 OREGON IS DUNKING ON OHIO STATE https://t.co/HtSjsF1As6
— College Football Report (@CFBReport) November 7, 2026 
 Down geaux the Tigers! Alabama bests LSU in Baton Rouge
 Many were questioning Alabama’s position at No. 5 in the initial College Football Playoff rankings.  
 Alabama was not questioning it, though  — the Tide rolled No. 14 LSU in Death Valley , 31-13, and dealt a massive blow to LSU’s playoff hopes. Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell had an efficient day, going 17-for-24 for 206 yards and three touchdowns, averaging 8.6 yards per attempt.  
 A thing of beauty 😮‍💨 📺: ABC https://t.co/6fVD08bwQa
— Alabama Football (@AlabamaFTBL) November 7, 2026 
 LSU falls to 6-3 on the season while Alabama improves to 7-2 with games against Vanderbilt, Chattanooga and Auburn remaining. LSU hosts Texas next week before hitting the road to play Tennessee and Arkansas. 
 Notably, Lane Kiffin remains winless against Alabama all-time as a head coach.
 share with Facebook copy link 11:23 pm, November 7, 2026 Montana RB Eli Gillman's record-breaking day steals the show
 Move over Cooper Kupp! The Super Bowl MVP's Big Sky total touchdown record now belongs to Montana running back Eli Gillman after his four-touchdown performance brought his career total to 78. All four of Gillman's touchdowns came on the ground, where he added 196 yards on just eight carries. He also caught a 48-yard pass in Montana's 57-24 win. 
 THERE IT IS! A historic run for @eli_gillman to break @CooperKupp's @BigSkyConf record for total TDs with 78! #GoGriz https://t.co/c8um7CBgru
— Montana Griz Football (@MontanaGrizFB) November 7, 2026 
 The next record for Gillman to break belongs to former Villanova running back and Philadelphia Eagles star Brian Westbrook. Westbrook scored 89 total touchdowns during his time in the FCS, an all-time best.
 share with Facebook copy link 11:01 pm, November 7, 2026 Big-time ranked games coming up tonight
 We have two ranked-vs.-ranked games going on at the moment with  Alabama vs. LSU and  Oregon vs. Ohio State , but there are a few more we’re keeping our eyes on tonight that could have massive College Football Playoff implications. 
 No. 6 Kentucky at No. 13 Tennessee | 6:15 p.m. ET | ESPN 
 Who would have thought back in September that this would be one of the biggest SEC games of the season? 
 No. 13 Tennessee currently sits just outside of the projected CFP bracket; a win tonight would be huge for the Volunteers’ playoff hopes. Meanwhile, No. 6 Kentucky is looking for its first win over Tennessee since Oct. 17, 2020. 
 This game is the first of a three-game gauntlet for the Wildcats, who host Florida next weekend before traveling to play Missouri the following week. 
 No. 2 Georgia at No. 10 Ole Miss | 7:30 p.m. ET | ABC 
 Gunner Stockton and the Bulldogs head to Oxford to take on Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels of Ole Miss. Georgia is looking to avenge their loss in last year’s CFP, and Kirby Smart looks to get his first win in Oxford as head coach of the Dawgs (0-2).
 Meanwhile, No. 10 Ole Miss looks to avoid falling to 6-3 on the season, as three losses would make it tough for the Rebels to stay in the CFP picture. 
 No. 1 Miami (Fla.) at No. 11 Notre Dame | 7:30 p.m. ET | NBC 
 At 7-1, No. 11 Notre Dame currently sits right on the edge of the CFP picture — a reminder that the Irish just need to be ranked in the top-12 to make the CFP. 
 This is a big turning point in Notre Dame’s season, as a win over the No. 1 Hurricanes would likely propel the Irish firmly into the playoff picture. However, a loss could be fatal, as Notre Dame’s last remaining games would be Boston College, SMU and Syracuse. 
 On the other side, Miami will try to hold onto its No. 1 ranking and undefeated record and make it three-straight wins over the Irish since 2017. 
 share with Facebook copy link 10:24 pm, November 7, 2026 63-yard FG breaks DIII record
 Brevard College's Alex Araneda drilled a 63-yard field goal to open the scoring against Methodist, breaking the record for the longest field goal in DIII history.
 Check it out.
 Football: WATCH Alex Araneda's NCAA Division 3 all-time record-breaking 63-yard field goal in BC's 48-3 victory over Methodist at Ives-Lemel Family Field! #NadoNation #d3fb #SCTop10 @ESPNAssignDesk @SportsCenter https://t.co/goiTLNJzdA
— Brevard College Athletics (@BCTornados) November 7, 2026 
 The kick beat the old mark of 62 yards by Matthew Aven from Claremont-Mudd-Scripps in 2013.
 The longest made field goal in college football history — at any level — is 69 yards.  Abilene Christian's Ove Johansson set the record on Oct. 16, 1976. 
 share with Facebook copy link 10:00 pm, November 7, 2026 Catching up on the afternoon (so far)
 We’re here to loop you all in on some scores, moments and stats from the half of the 3:30 games.
 No. 23 Oregon 17 ,  No. 12 Ohio State 14 
 The Buckeyes defense nearly held the Ducks before heading into the locker room, but Oregon found their way to the endzone with two seconds left in the half to pull ahead. 
 Buckeyes quarterback Luke Fahey, who's stepped up for an injured Julian Sayin, is 13-of-19 for 143 passing yards without a touchdown.
 Anchored by Bo Jackson's two touchdowns on eight carries, Ohio State has been reliant on their ability to run the football.
 Starting off the scoring with a kiss to the crowd ‼️ @BoJackson2025 | #GoBucks https://t.co/O1rOHtxtC3
— Ohio State Football (@OhioStateFB) November 7, 2026 
 No. 5 Alabama 10, No. 14 LSU 3 
 Despite Ryan Coleman-Williams undergoing arthroscopic knee surgery on Oct. 17 to repair a meniscus injury following Alabama's 20-17 loss to Georgia, the Crimson Tide's star offensive weapon has shown no signs of slowing down.
 Coleman-Williams nabbed Alabama's lone touchdown of the half, but this time, on the ground. The receiver's routes have been limited to foster his ongoing recovery.
 UNO🤫 @Ryanwms1 📺: ABC https://t.co/yVxGw4JFoj
— Alabama Football (@AlabamaFTBL) November 7, 2026 
 No. 21 South Carolina 7, Texas A&M 9 
 South Carolina’s LaNorris Sellers left the SEC matchup during the second quarter after taking a sack and losing the football, injuring what appeared to be his ankle. 
 After a brief visit to the injury tent, Sellers headed for the locker room with a trainer.
 Sellers, who is 14-of-22 for 202 passing yards and a touchdown, returned to the field in the third quarter.
 Welcome to the endzone 👏 https://t.co/XTNNqIwjhR
— South Carolina Football (@GamecockFB) November 7, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 9:07 pm, November 7, 2026 Ferris State ties DII football record with 40th consecutive win
 With a 80-0 win over Wayne State (MI) , Ferris State notched their 40th consecutive victory , tying Grand Valley State’s DII record.
 The Bulldogs have not lost a game since Aug. 31, 2024, holding the longest active win streak in all the NCAA.
 Marcel Jones led Ferris State's offense with 134 rushing yards and four touchdowns.
